thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> Severity: P1. Alert: staging rollout - elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (5m window > 6%). PD: INC-184321. Routing: SRE-oncall. Telemetry: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/alerts/184321

maria: Acked. I'm on it, joining the call.

alex: oncall here, seeing spike from canary namespace staging-eu-3. p95 latency unchanged, p50 fine, but errors are 502/504 from embed proxy.

james: any customer-facing impact yet? CS / billing?

emily: CS ping: a couple of enterprise sandboxes reported timeouts for generation requests, one support ticket opened (TKT-992). Low volume but reproducible.

maria: good to know. hypothesis: new routing for tokenizer sharding landed in today's staging rollout. I can switch traffic away from staging-eu-3 to staging-eu-1 for the canary fraction.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: INC-184321 assigned to maria. Escalation policy active: if unacked for 2m will escalate to SRE TL.

alex: maria, can you run quick healthcheck dump? `kubectl -n staging-eu-3 get pods -l app=inference -o wide` and `curl -s http://staging-eu-3/api/health | jq .`

maria: running now. output snippet:
```
$ kubectl -n staging-eu-3 get pods -l app=inference
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-quant-7f8b9d6b8-9xk2p    1/1     Running   0          2h
inference-quant-7f8b9d6b8-bm4q7    1/1     CrashLoop 5          1h
```
```
$ curl -s http://staging-eu-3/api/health
{ "status": "degraded", "errors": { "embed-proxy": "504 gateway timeout" } }
```

maria: seeing crashloops on one replica, logs show repeated `kv-cache: assertion failed` followed by network timeouts to embed-proxy.

alex: that's consistent with the 504s. I suspect the new sharding produced a hot-path to embed-proxy and we hit connection limits.

james: recommend immediate mitigation: 1) scale down canary fraction to 0, 2) divert staging traffic, or 3) rollback the routing change. Which is fastest?

emily: customers on sandboxes want a quick fix; prefer divert + investigate.

maria: I'll update rollout to 0% for canary and re-route traffic. Command: `redwood rollout set --env=staging --canary=0 --policy=immediate`

alex: i can push a temporary iptables bump on embed-proxy side to raise conn limit while we divert. want me to do that?

maria: do the divert first so we don't risk touching prodish proxies. Executing now: `redwood traffic split --env=staging --from=staging-eu-3 --to=staging-eu-1 --percent=100`

incident-bot: traffic split job initiated: job-id ts-184321-1. Estimated propagation ~30s.

maria: traffic now at 100% to staging-eu-1 for canary. monitoring...

alex: embed-proxy 504s dropping in metrics. error rate for /v1/generate back down to baseline in ~45s. p99 latency still a bit high on eu-1 but stable.

emily: CS: updated ticket TKT-992 with mitigation note, asking customer to retry.

james: good. next steps: collect logs from crashlooping pod, triage root cause. If we can patch quick (revert tokenizer sharding config), do that; otherwise keep rollout halted.

maria: grabbing logs: `kubectl -n staging-eu-3 logs inference-quant-7f8b9d6b8-bm4q7` -> shows kv-cache eviction race on startup when embed-proxy responds slowly. Suspect client-side backpressure missing.

alex: can we increase embed-proxy connection pool or add timeouts? short-term, bump conn limit + backoff might help but needs QA.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: 15m unresolved -> escalation to SRE TL in 5m.

maria: i'm handing off to alex for the next 30m — need to step offline briefly. alex, you have the mitigation baton. i'll follow up and own postmortem.

alex: taking over. actions: 1) keep canary at 0, 2) apply conn limit increase to embed-proxy in staging-eu-3: `ansible-playbook playbooks/embed-proxy/conn-bump.yml --limit=staging-eu-3 --extra-vars 'max_conn=20000'`, 3) monitor for crashloop self-heal.

incident-bot: alex acknowledged. PagerDuty note updated.

alex: applied conn bump, restarted embed-proxy pod. pods show `READY 1/1`, crashlooping inference pod restarted and stabilized. logs show no further kv-cache assertion.

emily: CS: TKT-992 user confirms retries now succeed. marking as service restored on their end.

james: are we comfortable keeping the rollout halted or do we want to rollback the tokenizer sharding change from today's staging commit?

maria: since the immediate mitigation stabilised and crashloop appears fixed with conn bump, recommend rollback the routing change in the repo (safer) before re-enabling canary. I'll file a PR to revert the sharding flag and request quick review.

alex: agreed. I'll hold traffic split and only re-enable canary after the revert PR is merged + smoke test.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-184321 status -> mitigated. No customer SLA breach detected. Incident will remain open for postmortem until one is filed.

maria: assigning postmortem owner: maria. Will include timeline, root cause (routing change -> embed-proxy connection hotspot -> kv-cache evictions), remediation (revert, add backpressure & client timeouts, add canary throttling), and follow-ups (improve telemetry for embed-proxy backlog).

alex: next oncall for EU is james in ~2h, i'll brief him before handoff.

james: thanks. brief note for handover: watch for latent p99s on eu-1 after canary re-enable.

maria: closing operational thread here. i'll post postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-184321 marked mitigated at 1843211500.
